request.deadline: Staged liquidity deployment over three months after enactment, with monthly reporting; exact final delivery deadline not stated in document.
deliverables: BTC reserve architecture with transparent safety mechanisms
Composable FIRE and ICE Cardano-native assets
Open-source SDKs and adapters for wallets, DEXs, and DeFi protocols
Always-on public dashboards for reserve ratio, asset supply, liquidity health, fee flows, and deployment status
Monthly governance reports and reporting standards
Independent security review, audit, and economic modeling
Staged launch liquidity deployed over three months
Legal/compliance work, documentation, DRep communications, partner activation, and launch coordination
request.recipient: Intersect is proposed as interim fund administrator subject to confirmation and final agreement; Sundial remains accountable for deployment and delivery with Charms as technical partner.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Alchemy, a Cardano-native Bitcoin treasury protocol and BTCfi infrastructure layer by Sundial Protocol and Charms.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 10,000,000 ada, using an approximate USD 0.20 per ada reference value for an approximately USD 2.0 million planning budget split into two approximately USD 1.0 million pools.

Pool 1 would provide protocol infrastructure and staged launch liquidity, kept separate from operating spend and deployed in three monthly tranches of approximately USD 250,000, USD 250,000, and USD 500,000.

Pool 2 would fund delivery, audit, integrations, dashboards, governance reporting, legal/compliance work, and go-to-market execution with itemized planning allocations totaling approximately USD 1.0 million.

The proposal says profits, yield, and returns from treasury-supported launch liquidity will be returned to the Cardano Treasury quarterly, while principal may be returned only after a 30-day time-weighted average TVL of at least USD 60 million and a later governance approval.

Alchemy would use a shared BTC reserve backing FIRE and ICE, with reserve ratio formula (V x P) / L, FIRE price formula ((V x P) - L) / N+, an initial 5.0x target reserve ratio, and safety zones above 4.0x, between 2.0x and 4.0x, and below 2.0x.

FIRE is described as a volatility-absorbing residual BTC reserve claim with first-loss downside and upside exposure, while ICE is described as a USD-denominated BTC-backed asset intended for lower-volatility exposure with growth potential.

The proposer asserts Cardano currently lacks a serious production BTCfi infrastructure layer and that failure to pass the proposal would leave Bitcoin-backed structured exposure to consolidate on other chains and off-chain markets.

The proposal cites external references and market examples, including Strategy Q1 2026 results, Strategy BTC holdings and proceeds figures, Strive SATA activity, and on-chain products such as Apyx, Saturn, and Pendle, to support demand for BTC-backed structured exposure.

The proposal identifies material risks from BTC volatility, oracle/bridge/Charms protocol vulnerabilities, novel asset risk, delivery risk, and adoption risk, and proposes mitigations including overcollateralization, security review, economic modeling, staged deployment, dashboards, pause rules, legal/compliance work, reporting, and administrator oversight.

Intersect is proposed as interim fund administrator, with auditable accounts, auto-abstain delegation for administrator-held ada, fund separation, milestone verification, reporting, and custody controls, but confirmation and final agreement are still pending.

summary: The document requests 10,000,000 ada for a milestone-gated BTCfi protocol and launch-liquidity package, with detailed budget pools, technical mechanics, reporting and oversight commitments, identified risks, and several independently checkable but not fully evidenced market-demand references.
